name: Los Angeles
tagline: Sunshine, Beaches, and the Entertainment Capital of the World
description: Los Angeles offers FIRE retirees 284 days of sunshine, world-class beaches, and a creative energy found nowhere else. The sprawling metropolis demands a car, which adds cost, but rewards with incredible ethnic food diversity, hiking in the Santa Monica Mountains, and a laid-back lifestyle that makes every day feel like vacation. California's state income tax hits portfolios hard, but the weather, culture, and outdoor access create an undeniable quality of life.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 200-1000 Mbps fiber available via AT&T and Spectrum
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderately Safe — varies widely by neighborhood; many areas are very safe with typical big-city awareness needed
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) — 25 min from downtown; Burbank (BUR) — 20 min from Hollywood
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with dry, warm summers (25-35°C) and mild, occasionally wet winters (10-18°C). Sunshine 284 days per year.

housing.description: The cheapest habitable studio in Koreatown, East Hollywood, or the San Fernando Valley, well inland from the beach

dining.description: Home cooking plus LA's cheap eats — taco trucks, K-Town counters, and San Gabriel Valley noodle houses

healthcare.description: Subsidized Covered California individual plan under the ~400%-FPL cliff (a modest CA state subsidy assists); a sticky floor. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with CA insurance and gas — essentially mandatory in a city built for driving

entertainment.description: The free city — Runyon Canyon, Griffith Park, and beach days in Venice and Santa Monica

1M.lifestyle: A modest but real Los Angeles life. Housing is the cheapest habitable studio in Koreatown, East Hollywood, or the San Fernando Valley, well inland from the beach. A paid-off used car is non-negotiable in a city built for driving, and it — plus a subsidized marketplace health plan — anchors the budget. Meals lean on cooking at home and LA's unbeatable cheap eats: taco trucks, K-Town counters, and San Gabriel Valley noodle houses. Entertainment is the free city: Runyon Canyon, Griffith Park, and beach days in Venice and Santa Monica. Careful, but sunny and genuinely livable.

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable Westside-adjacent life in a well-located one-bedroom in Silver Lake, Mar Vista, or a similar neighborhood with real personality and some coastal proximity. Dining out regularly at the city's mid-range restaurants, a newer car for weekend runs up the PCH to Santa Barbara or out to Joshua Tree, and a mid-tier private health plan round out a life with genuine breathing room. California's income tax is a persistent headwind, but the day-to-day is easy and sun-soaked.

10M.lifestyle: Established Los Angeles luxury, anchored by a top-tier 2-bedroom in the Hollywood Hills or a Century City high-rise with skyline or ocean views. A private chef several nights a week, a luxury car with occasional car service, full household help, and concierge medicine at UCLA or Cedars are all routine, as is first-class travel and a standing presence on the arts-and-events circuit. This is comfortable, unbothered wealth in a city where the weather and outdoor access are the real luxury — even after California's top tax bite.
